name: Meditation Basics
description: A short guided pause: settle, notice your breath, and return gently to the present. It is a relaxing practice you can stop at any time. It is not a treatment for any condition.

steps.text: Sit or lie comfortably and let your eyes rest closed or softly lowered.
Notice the feeling of your body where it touches the chair or the floor.
Let your attention rest on the breath coming in and going out, without changing it.
When your mind wanders, notice that gently and bring your attention back to the breath.
End the pause by opening your eyes and noticing the sounds in the room.

claims.text: Noticing the body can be a simple way to feel more grounded in the present moment.
Paying gentle attention to the breath may help some people feel calmer for a short time.
Returning attention after it wanders is a common part of many meditation practices.

safety_notes: Not medical advice and not a treatment for any medical or mental health condition.
Stop if the practice feels distressing, and open your eyes or move as you like.
Do not practise while driving or operating machinery.
If you have a health condition, ask a clinician before starting a new practice.
